posts.name: 31-world-crocodile-asteroid
posts.caption:
An asteroid wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. Crocodiles came through it, and new research says warm refuges near the equator are a big part of why 🐊

The team reconstructed the temperature and rainfall preferences of over 400 crocodile-line species across 245 million years, then ran climate simulations of the years after the impact. Heat was probably only one reason they made it: small bodies, water, flexible diets and very low energy needs all helped too.

Source: Chiarenza, Howard, Varnham, Farnsworth, Valdes, Mannion (University College London), “Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs”, Science Advances, 2026.
